title: Binary search
useWhen: Search sorted data or locate a monotone boundary.
invariant: The target, if present, stays inside [lo, hi].
pitfall: A binary search on the answer requires a monotone feasibility predicate.

steps.label: Keep the upper half
steps.detail: 19 matches the target; its index is 5.

title: Two pointers
useWhen: Find a pair or maintain boundaries in sorted data.
invariant: Every discarded endpoint is impossible for the remaining search.
pitfall: Moving endpoints by sum assumes the array is sorted.

title: Sliding window
useWhen: Reuse aggregate work across contiguous fixed-width ranges.
invariant: The running sum contains exactly the current three elements.
pitfall: Variable windows with sum thresholds need additional assumptions if negatives occur.

title: Prefix sums
useWhen: Answer many range-sum queries after preprocessing.
invariant: prefix[i] is the sum of values before index i.
pitfall: For inclusive [l,r], subtract prefix[l] from prefix[r+1].

steps.label: Accumulate
steps.detail: Append the sum after each element.

title: Hashing & complement lookup
useWhen: Replace repeated pair searches with a lookup of earlier values.
invariant: The table stores only indices processed before the current value.
pitfall: Check the complement before insertion so one element is not used twice.

steps.label: Read 2
steps.detail: Need 7; it is not yet in the table.

title: Kadane’s algorithm
useWhen: Find a maximum-sum nonempty contiguous subarray.
invariant: Ending here is the best sum whose right endpoint is the current index.
pitfall: Initialize from the first element to handle all-negative input.

steps.label: Start
steps.detail: The only nonempty interval ends at −2.

title: Merge sort
useWhen: Sort with predictable O(n log n) time.
invariant: Each merged output prefix is sorted and contains the smallest consumed values.
pitfall: Merging needs both halves to be sorted first.

title: Three-way partition
useWhen: Partition values into three categories in one scan.
invariant: [0,low) are zero; [low,mid) are one; (high,n) are two.
pitfall: After swapping with high, inspect the incoming value before advancing mid.

steps.label: Move a 2 right
steps.detail: Swap mid=0 with high=4; decrease high.

steps.label: Move zeros left
steps.detail: Both zeros join the finished low region.

steps.label: Finish
steps.detail: The final 2 is already at high; decrease high.

title: Reverse a linked list
useWhen: Reverse links while keeping all nodes reachable.
invariant: prev owns the reversed prefix; current starts the remaining suffix.
pitfall: Save next before changing current.next.

title: Fast & slow pointers
useWhen: Detect a cycle without storing every visited node.
invariant: Inside a cycle, fast gains one position on slow per iteration.
pitfall: Check fast and fast.next before moving two steps.

steps.label: First move
steps.detail: Slow advances one edge; fast advances two.

steps.label: Meet
steps.detail: Both pointers reach 3. A cycle exists.

title: Monotonic stack
useWhen: Find the next greater value for many positions.
invariant: The stack contains unresolved indices in non-increasing value order.
pitfall: Store indices when outputs depend on positions or distances.

steps.label: Push 2
steps.detail: No later greater value is known.

steps.label: Resolve both
steps.detail: 3 is greater than 1 and 2; pop each once.

title: Monotonic deque
useWhen: Track each sliding window’s maximum.
invariant: Indices remain in the window and values decrease from front to back.
pitfall: Expire indices by position; equal values still need a consistent tie rule.

steps.label: First full window
steps.detail: Append index 2; the front gives maximum 3.

steps.label: New maximum
steps.detail: Expire index 1, then 5 removes smaller values from the back.

pitfall: A skewed tree can have height n; an explicit stack avoids recursive stack exhaustion.

title: Tree preorder
useWhen: Traverse a binary tree with a defined processing order.
invariant: Node → left → right; visit each parent before its descendants.
pitfall: A skewed tree can have height n; an explicit stack avoids recursive stack exhaustion.

title: Tree postorder
useWhen: Traverse a binary tree with a defined processing order.
invariant: Left → right → node; combine children before processing the parent.
pitfall: A skewed tree can have height n; an explicit stack avoids recursive stack exhaustion.

steps.detail: Left → right → node; combine children before processing the parent.

title: Tree level-order BFS
useWhen: Group binary-tree values by depth.
invariant: The queue begins each round with exactly one level.
pitfall: Capture the queue size before appending the next level.

steps.label: Second level
steps.detail: Read the two nodes that were present at the round start.

steps.label: Leaf level

title: BST search
useWhen: Locate a value using a binary-search-tree ordering invariant.
invariant: All values left of a node are smaller; all right values are larger under this contract.
pitfall: An unbalanced BST can degrade to O(n) search.

title: Trie insert & prefix search
useWhen: Share common prefixes across a dictionary.
invariant: A root-to-node path spells one prefix; an end marker distinguishes a word.
pitfall: A prefix match is not necessarily a complete-word match.

steps.label: Insert cat
steps.detail: Create c→a→t and mark t as a word end.

steps.label: Insert car
steps.detail: Reuse c→a, then add r with an end marker.

steps.label: Find prefix ca
steps.detail: c and a exist; the prefix matches.

steps.label: Find word car
steps.detail: The path exists and r is marked.

title: Heap / top-k
useWhen: Keep the k largest values seen in a stream.
invariant: A min-heap of size k holds the k largest processed values.
pitfall: The root is the kth largest only once k values have been retained.

steps.label: Read 3
steps.detail: 3 cannot improve the current top two.

title: Graph BFS
useWhen: Explore unweighted graphs in distance layers.
invariant: A vertex is marked on enqueue, so it enters the queue at most once.
pitfall: BFS minimizes edge count only when each edge has equal cost.

steps.label: Discover A
steps.detail: Enqueue source and mark it visited.

steps.label: Expand A
steps.detail: Discover B and C at distance 1.

title: Graph DFS
useWhen: Explore a branch deeply before returning to other neighbors.
invariant: The active call stack is a path; each vertex is entered only once.
pitfall: Directed cycle detection also needs active-stack state, not just visited.

steps.label: Enter A
steps.detail: Neighbors will be considered in insertion order B then C.

steps.label: Visit D
steps.detail: D has no unvisited neighbor; return to B then A.

steps.label: Descend C
steps.detail: Resume at A and visit C.

title: Grid flood fill
useWhen: Model a rectangular board as an implicit graph.
invariant: Each discovered cell receives the new color before it can be revisited.
pitfall: Explicitly choose four-way versus eight-way adjacency.

steps.label: Discover neighbors
steps.detail: Only (0,1) and (1,0) are connected matching neighbors.

steps.label: Component finished
steps.detail: The diagonal lower-right component remains unchanged.

title: Topological sort / Kahn
useWhen: Order prerequisites in a directed acyclic graph.
invariant: Only vertices with no remaining incoming edges are ready.
pitfall: If fewer than V vertices are emitted, a directed cycle remains.

title: Dijkstra shortest paths
useWhen: Compute shortest distances with nonnegative edge weights.
invariant: The smallest unsettled distance is final when removed from the priority queue.
pitfall: Negative edges break the settling argument; skip stale heap entries.

steps.label: Settle C
steps.detail: C→B (2) improves B to 3; C→D (5) gives 6.

steps.label: Settle D
steps.detail: Skip any later stale heap entries.

title: Bellman–Ford
useWhen: Handle negative edges and detect reachable negative cycles.
invariant: After k complete passes, shortest walks using at most k edges are represented.
pitfall: Only a negative cycle reachable from the source affects single-source distances.

steps.label: Initialize
steps.detail: Start at A; others are unreachable.

steps.label: Check for change
steps.detail: A second pass changes nothing; no further relaxation is possible.

title: Floyd–Warshall
useWhen: Compute all-pairs shortest paths on modest dense graphs.
invariant: At phase k, only processed vertices may be internal path vertices.
pitfall: Guard infinity before adding distances; negative diagonal entries signal a negative cycle.

title: Disjoint set union
useWhen: Maintain connectivity as components merge.
invariant: Every vertex reaches its component representative through parent links.
pitfall: DSU alone cannot remove edges or answer arbitrary dynamic deletions.

steps.label: Singletons
steps.detail: Each vertex is its own component.

steps.label: Union 0 and 1
steps.detail: Attach one representative to the other.

steps.label: Union 1 and 3
steps.detail: Find roots 0 and 2, then merge them.

title: Kruskal minimum spanning tree
useWhen: Connect all vertices with minimum total edge weight.
invariant: Chosen edges form a forest; each accepted edge joins two different components.
pitfall: A disconnected graph yields a minimum spanning forest, not one spanning tree.

steps.label: Accept B—C
steps.detail: Connect the final component; total cost 3.

steps.label: Reject A—C
steps.detail: Both endpoints already share a component.

title: Backtracking subsets
useWhen: Enumerate choices while restoring shared mutable state.
invariant: The current path contains exactly the choices on the active recursion branch.
pitfall: Undo each mutation before returning to a sibling branch.

steps.label: Empty subset
steps.detail: Every branch begins from a valid partial choice.

title: DP: states & recurrence
useWhen: Count paths when the last move determines a smaller subproblem.
invariant: dp[i] counts all ways to reach i with steps of size one or two.
pitfall: The empty path contributes dp[0]=1.

steps.label: Base cases
steps.detail: There is one way to reach stair 0 and stair 1.

title: 0/1 knapsack
useWhen: Choose each item at most once under a capacity bound.
invariant: After processing an item, dp[c] uses only processed items.
pitfall: Iterate capacity downward so the current item cannot be used repeatedly.

steps.label: First item
steps.detail: Update capacities 4,3,2 from right to left.

steps.label: Second item
steps.detail: Update 4 then 3. The items cannot both fit.

title: Longest common subsequence
useWhen: Compare two sequences while allowing deletions.
invariant: dp[i][j] is the LCS length of the first i and j symbols.
pitfall: A subsequence need not be contiguous; substring uses a different recurrence.

steps.detail: Initialize the empty-prefix row to zeros.

title: LIS with binary search
useWhen: Find a strictly increasing subsequence length efficiently.
invariant: tails[k] is the smallest possible tail for a length k+1 subsequence.
pitfall: The tails array alone is not necessarily an actual subsequence; reconstruction needs predecessors.

steps.label: Read 1
steps.detail: Replace the tail with a smaller value.

title: Greedy interval scheduling
useWhen: Select the maximum count of non-overlapping intervals.
invariant: The selected compatible interval ends as early as possible.
pitfall: This example requires the next start to be strictly after the previous finish. Changing the goal to total value calls for weighted interval DP.

steps.detail: Sort by finish time. Meetings here require strictly separated endpoints.

steps.detail: 6 is strictly after 5. Three meetings fit.

title: XOR cancellation
useWhen: Find the unique integer when every other value appears exactly twice.
invariant: Equal values cancel because x XOR x = 0.
pitfall: This contract fails when duplicates do not occur exactly twice.

title: KMP string matching
useWhen: Search a pattern without restarting after each mismatch.
invariant: The matched prefix is also a suffix of the text processed so far.
pitfall: On mismatch, fall back through prefix lengths instead of resetting the text pointer.

steps.detail: Three pattern characters match at text indices 0..2.

title: K-way merge
useWhen: Merge multiple sorted sequences with one frontier item per sequence.
invariant: The heap contains the smallest unconsumed value from each active sequence.
pitfall: Advance only the sequence whose head was removed.

title: Multi-source BFS
useWhen: Expand several simultaneous sources in distance layers.
invariant: All cells in the current frontier share the same earliest arrival time.
pitfall: Mark cells when enqueued and account for cells that no source can reach.

title: Bipartite coloring
useWhen: Check whether adjacent vertices can always receive opposite colors.
invariant: Every examined edge connects different colors.
pitfall: Start a new traversal for every disconnected component.

title: DFS active-stack cycle detection
useWhen: Detect directed back edges without confusing them with cross edges.
invariant: Gray vertices are on the current DFS path; black vertices are fully processed.
pitfall: A visited vertex alone does not prove a directed cycle.

title: Lowest common ancestor
useWhen: Find where two root-to-node paths meet most deeply.
invariant: A subtree reports whether it contains either target or an already found ancestor.
pitfall: Define behavior when one target is absent; do not silently assume both exist.

title: Merge overlapping intervals
useWhen: Compress overlapping ranges after sorting by start.
invariant: The output contains disjoint merged intervals covering every processed input.
pitfall: Clarify whether touching endpoints count as overlap.

title: Unbounded coin-change DP
useWhen: Minimize the number of coins for a target amount.
invariant: dp[s] is the fewest coins among all choices that end at sum s.
pitfall: An unreachable state is not zero; use infinity and translate it at the boundary.

title: Edit distance
useWhen: Minimize insertions, deletions, and replacements between strings.
invariant: Each cell contains the best cost for its two prefixes.
pitfall: Do not confuse unit-cost edit distance with LCS or substring length.

title: Interval dynamic programming
useWhen: Try a split point when a problem combines two contiguous subranges.
invariant: Shorter intervals are solved before intervals that depend on them.
